title: A Crown for the Salt Anew
premise: Rafael Vasquez has survived fifteen years in the warded city of Corvel by stealing memories and bottling them as harmless charms, keeping her own past locked away. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish on the same night, she learns the court beneath the mountain has begun collecting souls to fuel an endless winter—and that fifteen years ago she sold her sister's soul to them to buy her own escape. To undo the bargain, Rafael must gather the found family she never meant to make, steal back what was sold, and finally face the memory she bottled deepest: that she chose herself over someone she loved. The story ends with Rafael trading her own stolen hoard of memories—every charm she's ever made—to ransom her sister's soul, letting the stars return and choosing, at last, to build a family that remembers everything, including her.
about_author: Ulyana Marchetti is a former archivist who grew up in coastal towns where the fog was said to carry the voices of the forgotten. She writes fantasy about memory, debt, and the families we assemble from strangers.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Hours
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A night of ordinary trade in Corvel: she sells a bottled first kiss, a mother's lullaby, a soldier's courage. We learn her rules—never steal from the desperate, never bottle her own past—and feel the loneliness beneath her competence. Emotional beat: comfort curdling into unease as the wards hum wrong.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The border wards fall with a sound like breaking glass; the sky goes starless and stays that way. Panic spreads, prices spike, and a hooded buyer offers Rafael a fortune to steal 'a soul, lightly used.' Emotional beat: dread—the invisible life she built is ending whether she likes it or not.

chapters.title: Salt on the Sill
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, introducing the found family: Odile the disgraced ward-smith, Tam the boy who remembers nothing but kindness, and Brannic, a retired wardens' captain who suspects what Rafael is. They shelter together as the city curfews. Emotional beat: wary warmth—family forming without permission.

chapters.title: What the Wards Remember
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Examining the fallen ward-stones, Odile finds a signature: memory-magic, Rafael's own craft, used to blind the city's defenses. She confronts Rafael privately. Emotional beat: betrayal blooming—Odile must decide whether Rafael is a culprit or a witness.

chapters.title: A Debt Fifteen Years Old
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Forced by Odile's questions, Rafael opens her deepest bottled memory: the night she sold her sister Sera's soul to the court beneath the mountain in exchange for passage out of a burning village. Emotional beat: shame surfacing after fifteen years of anesthesia.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Brannic recounts what the wardens' records say of the subterranean court: it pays in wishes and collects in souls, and its long winter is how it feeds. The starless sky means it has begun a harvest. Emotional beat: cold clarity—the stakes are not one soul but a whole season of them.

chapters.title: The Buyer with No Face
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The hooded buyer returns, revealed as a hollow-eyed servant of the court who recognizes Rafael's craft—and her name. It offers her Sera's location in exchange for stealing the court's rival: the city's founding charter-memory. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as rescue.

chapters.title: Lessons in Forgetting
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam, who lost his memory to the court years ago, teaches Rafael how the court's soul-ledgers work—what he remembers of the mountain's halls from before. Emotional beat: tenderness and grief; the victim becomes the map.

chapters.title: The Charter Heist
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael, Odile, and Brannic break into the Archive of Founding to steal the charter-memory. Rafael finds it already half-eaten—something else is feeding on Corvel's past. Emotional beat: vertigo; the enemy is already inside the walls.

chapters.title: Brannic's Choice
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. The wardens' remnant discovers the break-in and Brannic must choose: report his companions or burn his last honor with them. He forges the record. Emotional beat: loyalty outweighing duty, and the cost of that.

chapters.title: Down the Stair of Teeth
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Following Tam's memories, the four descend through an abandoned mine into the mountain's throat, past wards made of bottled screams. Rafael recognizes her own early, clumsy work. Emotional beat: horror of self-recognition—the court learned cruelty from thieves like her.

chapters.title: The Winter Court
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. They witness the court's hall: chandeliers of frozen starlight, courtiers wearing borrowed faces, and the Soul-Ledger, an iron book of every bargain. Odile maps its defenses while Rafael searches for Sera's name. Emotional beat: awe weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Sera, As She Is Now
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael finds Sera—not dead, but a courtier, her memories worn like fine gloves, serving the winter willingly because she remembers nothing else. Sera doesn't know her. Emotional beat: heartbreak sharper than hatred; the rescue must be wanted, not forced.

chapters.title: A Bargain Offered
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The court's sovereign, wearing Rafael's own mother's face, offers a trade: the charter-memory and Rafael's craft in exchange for Sera's freedom—and a place at court where Rafael need never feel guilt again. Emotional beat: the seduction of forgetting.

chapters.title: Tam Remembers
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Standing in the hall where he was unmade, Tam's stolen memories begin to return, triggered by the Ledger's proximity. He remembers his name, his mother, the deal he never agreed to. Emotional beat: grief and fury fused into purpose.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Weakness
chapters.summary: Odile and Brannic's POV, alternating. Odile realizes the Ledger must be fed memories to hold its entries—meaning Rafael's craft can write it as well as read it. They plan to overwrite Sera's debt. Emotional beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: What Rafael Bottled Deepest
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. To fuel the rewrite, Rafael must unstopper every charm she's hoarded—fifteen years of stolen moments—and pour them into the Ledger. She hesitates: without them, she is only the woman who sold her sister. Emotional beat: the cost of love made literal.

chapters.title: The Writing of the Book
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. In the heart of the winter court, Rafael pours her hoard into the Ledger while Odile holds the wards and Brannic holds the door. Sera's debt burns away—but the sovereign tears the sky's last starlight down to stop them. Emotional beat: climax—sacrifice against erasure.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Breaks
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs in quick succession. The Ledger, overfed with love instead of debt, cracks; the bottled stars spill back into the sky; the court's courtiers wake and scatter. The sovereign, unmasked as a hollow shell, crumbles. Emotional beat: catharsis—light returning like a held breath released.

chapters.title: Sera, As She Might Have Been
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Freed but hollow, Sera must decide who to be without the court's borrowed memories. Rafael offers her the one charm she kept back: a single memory of their childhood, saved from the hoard. Emotional beat: reconciliation without erasure—love that doesn't demand the past be perfect.

chapters.title: A Crown for the Salt Anew
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The city, starlit again, must rebuild its wards; the survivors of the court need stewards, not jailers. Rafael, Odile, Brannic, Tam, and Sera take the work together—crowned not by gold but by responsibility. Emotional beat: found family formalized into purpose.

chapters.title: Everything, Remembered
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, coda. Months later, Rafael opens a new shop—not selling forgetfulness but helping people carry what they'd rather drop. She writes her own memory into a charm and gives it to Sera: the whole truth of the sale, and the whole truth of the rescue. Emotional beat: peace earned—memory as gift, not wound.
